findings.title: Staleness warning fires on every run once the graph is tracked
findings.description:
The check is `meta.json.gitCommitHash != HEAD` (130-131), yet lines 186-188 say the graph files stay tracked. Committing the graph moves `HEAD` one commit past the recorded hash, so the warning fires permanently with distance ≥ 1 even when no source file changed. Every later docs-only commit, including the skill's own concept and analysis output, widens the distance. A warning that is always on cannot be "prominent" (133) and defeats the failure mode the section says it guards against.

- **Fix:** compare the changed paths in `gitCommitHash..HEAD`, excluding `.understand-anything/` and `project-documents/`, and honouring `.understandignore`.
- **Also undefined:** a recorded hash that is unreachable (rebase, squash, shallow clone), so no distance can be computed.
- **Also undefined:** a dirty working tree, which `HEAD` comparison cannot see.

findings.title: Hygiene step runs after the scratch exists and is skipped on the missing-graph path
findings.description:
Step 1 stops when the graph is missing and tells the user to run `/understand` (127-128). The `.gitignore` entry is step 2 (136-137), so it is never written on that path. `/understand` Phase 7 then creates `.trash-<epoch>/` (176-178) in a repo with no ignore entry, which is the path where "leave the working tree clean" (49-50) matters most. Hygiene must precede the precondition stop.

Related gaps in the same section:
- `intermediate/scan-result.json` (88) is neither ignored (183) nor in the tracked list (186).
- The edit leaves an uncommitted `.gitignore` change with no owner for the commit.
- Behaviour is unspecified when `.gitignore` is absent, the directory is not a git repo, or the user already ignores all of `.understand-anything/`. That last case invalidates the tracking and staleness reasoning.

findings.title: "Verify the plugin is installed" contradicts "graph is an input, not a dependency"
findings.description: Lines 56-58 make the graph plain data, and 186-188 make it tracked project knowledge. A teammate who clones the repo without the plugin therefore has everything the skill needs. Step 1 nonetheless requires the plugin to be installed. No mechanism is given for a markdown skill to detect a user-scope marketplace plugin (70-71). Drop the plugin check and precondition only on the graph file; mention the plugin only in the "graph missing" message.

findings.title: Graph extraction is specified as "grep" and the fields read do not cover the promised outputs
findings.description:
Step 3 (138-139) must select nodes by `type` and pull `layers[]` and `tour[]` out of a large JSON file. Grep cannot filter JSON structurally, and if the file is single-line a match returns the whole graph, which is exactly what the read discipline forbids. No structured extractor (`jq`, a Python one-liner, an `sq` helper) is named, so the hardest step is left to the model.

The data flow is also inconsistent with the outputs:
- Step 3 never reads `edges[]`, but the analysis doc promises "dependency observations" (153).
- Initial Technical Direction is sourced from "languages, frameworks, dependencies" (168), which no field in the stated contract supplies; `project`'s contents are never defined (85).
- "Entry points" (153) has no stated source.

findings.title: No validation of the graph contract beyond "file exists"
findings.description:
The contract is transcribed from v2.8.1 of a plugin the document calls "actively developed" (40-41). The only failure handled is a missing file (57, 128). Unspecified cases:
- A graph with no `tour[]` (Phase 6 failed or was skipped), which is the field the document calls critical (101-105).
- An empty `layers[]`, or renamed fields after an upstream release.

Under the project rule "never use silent fallback values" (`CLAUDE.md:8`), each needs an explicit stop or an explicit "not available" in the output.

Separately, `config.json` and `.understandignore` are listed as consumed (87, 89) but no flow step uses them. Either cut them or say what `outputLanguage` means when summaries are not in English.

findings.title: Initiative-plan candidates are under-specified and collide with "never fabricate intent"
findings.description:
The whole mechanism is "derived from layer boundaries and complexity clustering". Layers partition what exists; initiatives state what someone intends to do. The interview (140-142) asks about problem, users, business context and constraints, and never about goals or wanted work. Candidates are therefore either a retroactive relabelling of layers or invented intent, which 46-48 prohibits and 119 ("what should we do about this codebase?") invites.

Also undefined: the destination file, and what happens when `001-initiative-plan.{project}.md` already exists, as it does in this repo. State whether candidates are retroactive or forward-looking, add the interview questions that supply the intent, and name the write target.

findings.title: Capability 1 has no defined behaviour for existing artifacts or an unplanned repo
findings.description:
- **Existing concept or re-run:** a second run must either overwrite the sacred User-Provided Concept section (`CLAUDE.md:75-76`) or refuse. Neither is stated.
- **Motivating case:** a "codebase that was never planned in squadron" (21) has no `project-documents/user/` tree, no cf project and no frontmatter gate. Who creates the layout, and where `{project}` comes from (the graph's `project` field or cf), is unspecified.
- **Minor:** the section defined as the human's verbatim words will contain skill-authored question text and "unknown" markers (149, 171-172).

findings.title: Capability 2's no-concept path contradicts "derived, not authored" and leaves three fields without a source
findings.description:
The no-concept case is declared the tested path. In it, Problem, Audience and Approach (219-221) have the concept as their only listed source. Line 198 fills the gap with "initiative plan plus interview", but an interview answer is a new claim that exists in no approved artifact. That is what 51-52 and 234-235 forbid.

Capability 2 has no Flow section, so the interview is otherwise undefined: no questions, and no place the answers persist. Resolve it one way:
- write the answers into a concept document first and derive from that (this reuses Capability 1's interview), or
- mark those fields absent in the overview.

The concept is also found by exact filename `000-concept.{project}.md`, while this repo's plan cites `001-concept.squadron.md` (`project-documents/user/project-guides/001-initiative-plan.squadron.md:5`). Locate it by `docType: concept` so a differently indexed concept is not silently treated as missing.

findings.title: Status, Roadmap and Risks are sourced from fields that do not carry that information
Emphasis parameter is both present and deferred
findings.description: The translation rules say "Emphasis is a generation parameter". Resolved Design Decisions (328-331) say there is one neutral document and "an emphasis parameter is added only if real use demonstrates the need". Line 64 adds that audience separation is "not a tone setting". Delete 238-239 or rewrite it to match the resolved decision.

findings.title: Output Conventions misstate what is written, and the document sanctions a deviation from a convention it says it does not change
findings.description:
- **Wrong "both":** line 243 says both capabilities write to `user/analysis/` with `docType: analysis`. Capability 1's primary output is `project-guides/000-concept.{project}.md` with `docType: concept` (148), plus an initiative plan.
- **Overflow:** lines 245 and 333 claim "no change to `file-naming-conventions.md`" and "the 940-949 reserved range". Lines 254-258 then sanction overflow into 950+. That is a convention change, to a file Context Forge owns (`src/squadron/documents/schema.py:7`), and the document never says what 950+ is reserved for.
- **Existing uses:** 950 already means maintenance in this ecosystem (`CLAUDE.md.bak:64`, `950-tasks.maintenance.md`). The project `analyze` skill (`.claude/skills/analyze/SKILL.md:28-29`) is a third consumer of 940+ that Current State does not mention.

findings.title: Per-run index allocation creates the exhaustion the overflow rule then patches
findings.description:
"Each run is an independent sample" is true of tech-debt audits. It is false of an overview and a comprehension doc, which are revisions of one derived artifact. Per-run increments leave several overviews with no indication of which is current. The document's own reason for rejecting audience variants (328-330) is that multiple artifacts must each be kept true.

Regenerate in place under a stable name and bump `dateUpdated`. The overflow paragraph (254-258) then becomes unnecessary. The index is also model-chosen, a weakness slice 323 already recorded for the audit skill (`project-documents/user/slices/323-slice.tech-debt-audit-baseline-harness.md:75`).

findings.title: The stakeholder document is placed where it must carry the internal metadata the translation rules strip
findings.description:
Under `project-documents/user/` the overview needs an indexed filename and `docType`/`status` frontmatter. Lines 230-231 say indices and docType "never appear". The repo already has a boundary for external-reader documents: files outside `validate.docs_root`, such as `docs/QUICKSTART.md`, correctly have no frontmatter (`project-documents/user/slices/172-slice.sq-validate-docs-mechanical-frontmatter-enforcement.md:81-87`; `CLAUDE.md.bak:32`).

Writing to `docs/` satisfies "a document boundary, not a tone setting" (64), consumes no 94x index, and makes the gate argument at 245-247 moot for Capability 2. Reusing `analysis` is the workaround for a problem the placement creates.

findings.title: `*-analysis.*.md` in `user/analysis/` is already a code-level discriminator for audit files
findings.description: The reuse is presented as free. `src/squadron/metrology/audit.py:56-59` globs `project-documents/user/analysis/*-analysis.*.md`, and `find_audit_file` (259-283) returns the newest match as the tech-debt audit. `NNN-analysis.overview.md` and `NNN-analysis.codebase-comprehension.md` both match. The Dependencies section's "independent of … 320" (312-313) overlooks this shared filename namespace. Narrow the harness glob or choose a naming shape it does not match.

findings.title: Provenance and claim attribution are required but never defined
Skill name `understand` re-creates the surface confusion that slice 344 was deprecated for
findings.description:
`/analysis:understand` was the name planned for the vendored graph builder (`project-documents/user/architecture/340-arch.skill-pack-infrastructure.md:34`). Slice 344 was dropped partly for "a competing command surface" (`project-documents/user/slices/344-slice.add-understand-anything-to-analysis-pack.md:16`). Now a skill named `understand` that does not build a graph tells the user to run `/understand`.

"No collision" (276, 323) is asserted without evidence. The 340 spike tested dispatcher argument passing, not a marketplace plugin skill coexisting with `~/.claude/commands/analysis/understand.md`. Confirm in a live session that bare `/understand` still resolves to the plugin.

findings.title: Delivery and Dependencies understate the first-party command change
findings.description: Adding `commands/sq/overview.md` breaks `tests/cli/test_install_commands.py:123`, which asserts exactly 9 files. The `EXPECTED_COMMANDS` contract at 130-140 also expects every `/sq:*` file to reference an `sq` subcommand or dispatcher; a pure-prompt command is a new kind there. The dependency on [100] is described as "CLI command registration" (307), but neither capability registers a CLI command. The real dependency is the `sq install-commands` file copy.

findings.title: Interview scope is listed two different ways
findings.description: Step 4 lists "business context", which has no row in the section table (163-169). The table lists Development Approach / methodology (169), which step 4 omits. The translation-rule example "Initiative 140 status draft" (231) uses a status that line 261 says the gate rejects.
